title: Equivariant Serre pairings for homogeneous flag line bundles
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and $S$ a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with these terms as defined in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$, where $B$ is a Borel subgroup, with character lattice $X=X^*(T)$ and positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $N=|\Phi^+|$ and $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$. Let $B^-$ be the opposite Borel containing $T$, with roots $-\Phi^+$. For $y\in X$, extend $y$ to $B^-$ through its projection to $T$ and let $\mathcal L_y$ be the sheaf of sections of the homogeneous line bundle on $Q=S/B^-$ whose sections over $V$ are regular functions $f:\pi^{-1}(V)\to F$ satisfying $f(gb)=y(b)^{-1}f(g)$ after every commutative $F$-algebra extension, with $\pi:S\to Q$ the quotient. Write $H^i(y)=H^i(Q,\mathcal L_y)$ for Zariski sheaf cohomology with the induced left-translation $S$-action. Rational action means a counital coassociative coaction $V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$, and equivariance means the coaction identity. The canonical invertible sheaf $\omega_Q=\bigwedge^N\Omega^1_{Q/F}$, with its natural $S$-action, is $S$-equivariantly isomorphic to $\mathcal L_{-2\rho}$. Here $\Omega^1_{Q/F}$ denotes the sheaf representing $F$-linear derivations. There is an $S$-invariant linear trace $\operatorname{tr}:H^N(-2\rho)\to F$ such that for every $y\in X$ and $0\le i\le N$ the cup product followed by this trace is a perfect pairing of finite-dimensional rational $S$-modules
$$H^i(y)\times H^{N-i}(-y-2\rho)\longrightarrow F.$$
Perfect means that the maps from either factor to the linear dual of the other are bijective. The action on $F$ is trivial; invariance holds after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. This includes $N=0$, with the zeroth exterior power as the canonical line.

proof.text: The semisimple group $S$ is reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Apply [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts] with $B_0=B^-$ and $I=\varnothing$: $P_I=B^-$, the quotient $Q=S/B^-$ is proper of finite type, and $\pi:S\to Q$ is a faithfully flat finitely presented right $B^-$-torsor. The Borel is smooth. Thus [lem-sfb-homogeneous-cotangent-associated-bundle], with $G=S,H=B^-$, applies. For $V=(\mathfrak s/\mathfrak b^-)^\vee$ and $d=\dim_FV$, it gives smoothness of $Q$, pure dimension $d$, the equivariant identification $\Omega^1_{Q/F}\simeq S\times^{B^-}V$, and its determinant identification $\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{Q/F}\simeq S\times^{B^-}\bigwedge^dV$.

source.place: 7.15 and 7.16(c), pp.142--143; 18.11--18.14, pp.389--390; homogeneous cotangent and determinant specialization

proof.text: The weight decomposition in [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] and the Borel decomposition in [lem-sfb-borel-opposite-root-dichotomy] give $\mathfrak s=\mathfrak t\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak s_\alpha$ and $\mathfrak b^-=\mathfrak t\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in-\Phi^+}\mathfrak s_\alpha$. Each root space has dimension one by the first cited statement. Taking the quotient cancels exactly the toral and negative-root summands. Consequently $\mathfrak s/\mathfrak b^-$ has one-dimensional weight spaces $\alpha\in\Phi^+$, and $V$ has weights $-\alpha$. Therefore $d=N$ and the one-dimensional $B^-$-module $D=\bigwedge^NV$ restricts to the $T$-character $-\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha=-2\rho$. The wedge of a weight basis proves this determinant formula, including the empty basis for $N=0$.

source.place: 21.11(b),(c) and Corollary 21.13, pp.428--430; quotient and exterior-basis calculation

proof.text: Let $\chi:B^-\to\mathbf G_m$ be the action on $D$. Every root subgroup $U_\gamma$, $\gamma\in\Phi$, used in [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. A homomorphism $\mathbf G_a\to\mathbf G_m$ corresponds to a unit of $F[t]$, hence is a nonzero constant, and its value at $0$ forces that constant to be $1$. Thus $\chi$ is trivial on each negative root subgroup as a group-scheme morphism. The product coordinates of [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], used for $B^-$, imply it is trivial on $U^-=R_u(B^-)$. Since $B^-=U^-\rtimes T$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $\chi$ is exactly the extension of $-2\rho$ through $B^-\to T$. Choose a nonzero vector in $D$ to identify it with that character module. Step 1 identifies its associated line with $\omega_Q$. The associated-bundle convention there is $(g,z)b=(gb,\chi(b)^{-1}z)$, so its sections satisfy precisely $f(gb)=\chi(b)^{-1}f(g)$. We obtain the required $S$-equivariant isomorphism $\omega_Q\simeq\mathcal L_{-2\rho}$, with no sign change.

source.place: 18.11--18.14, pp.389--390; 21.11(c), pp.428--429; ordered root coordinates, with elementary polynomial-unit calculation

proof.text: For characters $a,b$, multiplication in the one-dimensional fibres gives $\mathcal L_a\otimes\mathcal L_b\simeq\mathcal L_{a+b}$: on a local section of $\pi$ these are free rank-one sheaves and the map sends the tensor of their basis elements to the basis element of the sum. On a change of section by $c\in B^-$ the two transition factors multiply, since $a(c)^{-1}b(c)^{-1}=(a+b)(c)^{-1}$; hence these local maps glue, with inverses on the same trivializations. They commute with left translations since multiplication of functions does. In particular $\mathcal L_y^\vee\otimes\omega_Q\simeq\mathcal L_{-y-2\rho}$ and evaluation is the multiplication map to $\mathcal L_{-2\rho}$. These lines are locally free and quasi-coherent, so [lem-sfb-linearized-qcoherent-cohomology-coaction] gives rational $S$-coactions on their cohomology; the induced action is the stipulated left-translation action. This applies because $Q$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and separated, and $S$ is affine of finite type.

source.place: 18.11--18.14, pp.389--390: local torsor sections and transition functions; cohomology coactions from the cited general node

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-proper-coherent-trace-pairing] to the smooth proper $F$-scheme $Q$ of pure dimension $N$ and the locally free line $\mathcal E=\mathcal L_y$. Compose the trace $t_Q:H^N(Q,\omega_Q)\to F$ with the cohomology map of the inverse of the isomorphism in step 3 to define $\operatorname{tr}:H^N(-2\rho)\to F$. Step 4 identifies its cup-evaluation pairing with exactly $H^i(y)\times H^{N-i}(-y-2\rho)\to F$ in the question. The cited theorem gives finite-dimensionality and bijectivity of both duality maps for every $0\leq i\leq N$.

source.place: Tags 0FVV (5),(7), 0FVW, 0FVY and 0FW0, smooth proper locally free specialization

proof.text: Fix any commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $s\in S(A)$. On $Q_A$ the inverse translation $h=L_{s^{-1}}$ and the bundle linearization identify $h^*\mathcal L_{y,A}$ with $\mathcal L_{y,A}$. The induced cohomology maps are exactly the evaluations of the rational coactions, by [lem-sfb-linearized-qcoherent-cohomology-coaction]. The dual linearization and differential on $\omega$ give the action on the second factor in step 4. The isomorphism $\omega_Q\simeq\mathcal L_{-2\rho}$ is $S$-equivariant by its associated-bundle construction, so the trace and pairing invariance under $h$ are exactly the automorphism-naturality assertions of [lem-sfb-smooth-proper-coherent-trace-pairing]. They give $\operatorname{tr}_A(s z)=\operatorname{tr}_A(z)$ and $P_A(su,sv)=P_A(u,v)$. Taking $A=F[S]$ and its universal point proves the corresponding coaction identities, and hence the requested invariance after every scalar extension. For $N=0$ all wedges and tensor identifications above use the empty wedge and $\omega_Q=\mathcal O_Q$; the same smooth proper theorem with $d=0$ applies, so no positive-dimension exception was introduced.
